# VibeCode QA brand kit

This folder is the **single source of truth** for VibeCode QA's visual identity.
Before it existed, the same favicon lived as two unrelated byte-identical copies
in two repos with no shared source, and the only real logo artwork lived inside
a Tauri build directory. If you need a mark, a favicon, a colour, or a social
card, take it from here.

**Nothing in this folder is generated by hand.** The root `favicon.svg`,
`og-image.svg` and `og-image.png` that the website serves are copies produced by
`build.mjs`. Edit the source in `brand/`, run the script, commit both.

---

## The name

| | |
|---|---|
| Canonical product name | **VibeCode QA** — two words, capital V, capital C, capital QA |
| Accepted short form | **VCQA**, in technical prose and identifiers only |
| npm scope | `@vibecodeqa` (`@vibecodeqa/cli`, `@vibecodeqa/mcp`) |
| Domain | `vibecodeqa.online` (dashboard: `app.vibecodeqa.online`) |

Never write **VibeCodeQA** (no space) or **Vibecode QA** (lowercase c). As of
2026-08-18 the website uses "VibeCode QA" 108 times and neither misspelling
appears once — keep it that way.

Use **VCQA** the way the standards pages already do: as shorthand inside a
sentence that has already established the product ("VCQA standards cite them,
then own the seam"). It is not a display name. It never appears in a headline,
a logo lockup, a page title, or an OG card.

---

## Provenance, and the missing vector

**There is no vector source for the ring mark. The 512×512 PNG is the master.**

This is stated first and plainly because a brand kit that implies a vector it
does not have is worse than one that admits the gap. `logo/icon-512.png` is a
byte-for-byte copy of `app/src-tauri/icons/icon.png`
(`sha256:6413bfe9…95d3`) — the Tauri desktop icon, and the only real logo
artwork that exists anywhere in the workspace. Every other raster in `logo/` is
downsampled from it. Nothing here was traced, redrawn, or auto-vectorised, and
no file in this folder claims to be the mark's geometry.

`logo/icon-avatar.svg` is the one SVG in `logo/`, and it is **not** a vector
master: it is a thin wrapper that places the PNG on an opaque background so
the avatar export is reproducible. Its own header says so.

### What would actually close this gap

A real source file needs to be, in order of preference:

1. The original design document the mark was drawn in (Figma, Illustrator,
   Affinity), exported to `logo/icon.svg` as paths, with the source file linked
   from this README. **If that document still exists somewhere, recovering it is
   the cheapest fix by a wide margin.**
2. Failing that, a deliberate redraw of the mark as SVG paths, done as its own
   piece of work with the output compared against `icon-512.png` at 512, 128 and
   32 px before it replaces anything.

Until one of those lands, treat the mark as raster-only. Practical consequences,
so nobody is surprised:

- The mark **cannot be recoloured** without redrawing it. Do not attempt it.
- The mark **cannot be scaled above 512 px** without softening. If you need
  print or a large hero, that is a blocker, not an inconvenience.
- The mark **cannot be used as an SVG favicon**, which is why the favicon is
  still the indigo `VQ` square. See "Two identities" below.

---

## Two identities (read this before "fixing" anything)

VibeCode QA currently ships two unrelated marks, and this kit does not pretend
otherwise:

| | Indigo `VQ` | Amber + cyan rings |
|---|---|---|
| Artwork | `favicon.svg` | `logo/icon-512.png` |
| Format | SVG, 249 bytes | PNG, raster only |
| Colours | `#818cf8` → `#6366f1` | `#ffc131`, `#24c8db` |
| Ships on | website, web app, all 17 site pages' favicon | desktop app dock icon, installers |

They share no colour (see `palette.md`). This was never a decision — the two
surfaces were simply built at different times. Both are therefore canonical **for
their own surface**, and this kit keeps them apart rather than blending them.

**Open decision, needs a human:** unify on one mark, or keep a wordmark for web
and a symbol for the app. Do not resolve it in a drive-by change — recolouring
the rings needs the vector that does not exist, and changing the web accent
touches 17 pages plus the dashboard.

---

## Which file do I use?

| I need… | Use | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **GitHub org / repo avatar** | `logo/icon-avatar-512.png` | 512×512, opaque `#09090b`. Flattened on purpose — GitHub composites avatars over both light and dark chrome, and a transparent mark reads inconsistently. |
| **The mark with transparency** | `logo/icon-512.png` | Or the 256/128/64/32 downsamples. Below 64 px the two rings start to merge; prefer the `VQ` square at 32 px and under. |
| **Website favicon** | `favicon.svg` | The source. The repo-root copy is generated; do not edit it. |
| **Website social card** | `og/og-image.png` | 1200×630 PNG. This is what `index.html` points `og:image` and `twitter:image` at. |
| **Editing the social card** | `og/og-image.svg` | The source. Re-render after editing (see below). |
| **A colour, any colour** | `palette.md` | Includes measured contrast ratios. |

### Why the OG image is a PNG

`index.html` used to point `og:image` at an **SVG**, and every major platform —
X/Twitter, Facebook, LinkedIn, Slack, Discord, iMessage — refuses SVG for
`og:image`. Link previews were silently falling back to no image at all. The SVG
is the editable source; **the PNG is what ships**. If you add a new social card
anywhere in this project, reference the PNG.

---

## Consuming this kit from another repo

The nine VCQA repos are separate git repositories with no shared package, so
consumption is a **vendored copy plus a recorded hash**, not an import. The rule
is simple: *copy the bytes, never edit the copy, record where it came from.*

### For `app` (the web app and desktop monitor)

`app/public/favicon.svg` is currently a byte-identical duplicate of this repo's
favicon with no recorded relationship to it. To adopt this kit:

1. **Favicon** — replace `app/public/favicon.svg` with the bytes of
   `vibecodeqa/brand/favicon.svg`.
   Expected content hash: `sha256:26feb2faa00e7c2404bf4ce9b19bc2f7ac3679c93642adf42b9fee8aa25f5018`
   (249 bytes). Since the two files are already identical today, this is a
   provenance change, not a visual one — the diff should be empty. Record the
   hash in `app` so future drift is detectable.

2. **Social card** — the dashboard is a different origin
   (`app.vibecodeqa.online`) and should get its **own** card, not this one.
   Copy `og/og-image.svg` as a starting template, change the headline and the
   card contents to describe the dashboard, then export to PNG at exactly
   **1200 × 630**, filename **`og-image.png`**, served from the app origin root
   (`app/public/og-image.png` → `https://app.vibecodeqa.online/og-image.png`).
   Point both `og:image` and `twitter:image` at the **`.png`**, with
   `twitter:card` = `summary_large_image`. Do not ship an SVG `og:image`.

3. **Desktop icons** — leave `app/src-tauri/icons/` exactly as it is. Tauri owns
   that directory and regenerates it; `logo/icon-512.png` here is the copy, and
   `src-tauri/icons/icon.png` remains the upstream. If the mark is ever
   redrawn, `src-tauri/icons/` is regenerated first and this folder re-copied
   from it, not the other way round.

### For any other repo

Take what you need, keep the filename, and note the source path and hash next to
the copy. If you find yourself editing a copy, stop — change it here instead.

---

## Regenerating

```bash
node brand/build.mjs           # regenerate the repo-root copies from brand/
node brand/build.mjs --check   # fail if a copy has drifted or an export is
                               #   missing / the wrong pixel size
node brand/build.mjs --render  # re-render the PNG exports from source
```

`--check` is pure Node with no dependencies and does not render anything, so it
is safe to run anywhere, including the deploy workflow. `--render` needs
`rsvg-convert` (`brew install librsvg`) and macOS `sips`; on this toolchain it
is byte-reproducible, so re-rendering an unchanged source produces no diff.

**`--check` is not yet wired into `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`.** It was left
out deliberately: that file had unrelated uncommitted changes in flight when
this kit landed, and editing it would have collided. Adding
`node brand/build.mjs --check` next to the other validators in the "Build docs"
step is a one-line follow-up and is the thing that makes the generated copies
genuinely enforced rather than merely conventional.

### After editing `og/og-image.svg`

Render it, then **look at the result at thumbnail size** — around 400 px wide is
what Slack and X actually show. Text that is comfortable at 1200 px routinely
turns to mush at 400. The current card was checked at both.

Note that `og-image.svg` is rendered by librsvg, not a browser, so it must not
rely on anything librsvg cannot do: no CSS `@import`, no webfonts, no
`foreignObject`. The font stack is `Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, 'Helvetica
Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif` — librsvg resolves it to Helvetica Neue on
macOS, browsers resolve it to Inter or the system UI font, and the layout
tolerates both.

---

## Do / don't

**Do**

- Take colours from `palette.md`, which lists only values that actually ship.
- Keep the mark on `#09090b` or on transparency.
- Give the mark room — the artwork sits in a 376 × 423 box inside its 512 × 512
  canvas, and that ~13% padding is part of the design. Do not crop it out.
- Use the PNG for any `og:image`.

**Don't**

- Don't edit the root `favicon.svg`, `og-image.svg` or `og-image.png` — they are
  generated. `build.mjs --check` will catch you.
- Don't recolour, rotate, skew, add effects to, or place the mark on a busy
  photographic background.
- Don't set the `VQ` mark's letters in a different typeface; it is a fixed
  lockup, not a template.
- Don't introduce a third identity. Two is already one too many.
- Don't auto-vectorise `icon-512.png` and commit the result as `icon.svg`. A
  traced approximation presented as a master is exactly the problem this folder
  exists to end.
